newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends softer in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends softer in thin dealings.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended softer at C$1.3925 (US$0.7181) on Thursday from this morning's opening of C$1.3913 (US$0.7187), but stronger than Wednesday's close of C$1.3930 (US$0.7178), traders said.
* They said some bullish sentiment toward the Canadian dollar emerged after Wednesday comments from the Bank of Canada.

The trader said there was an underlying weakness in the the Canadian dollar market because of the uncertainty over whether the Bank of Canada would follow a possible rise in U.S. short-term rates in May.

Some market players have speculated the U.S. Federal Reserve could raise short-term interest rates as early as May, widening the interest rate spread between Canada and the United States if the Bank of Canada refused to follow.
Traders said wider spreads would prod international investors to sell off their Canadian dollar denominated short-term debt-holdings, weakening the Canadian dollar.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.2315 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.2294 and reached 90.53 yen from 90.44.
